title: Agent Constraints for Memory Quality Lab Triage
description: Defines what an AI coding agent may and may not do during triage and fix proposal.

may: Read redacted quality-lab reports, fixture YAML, and relevant product source files.
Identify the most likely failure category (ADMISSION, CONSOLIDATION, ROUTING, RETRIEVAL, PROTOCOL, PROMPT, FALLBACK, SAFETY_PRIVACY) and relevant code area.
Propose a minimal new test fixture that isolates the observed defect.
Propose a narrowly scoped code patch description (not auto-apply).
Run scripts/run-memory-eval.sh as the existing deterministic gate.
Run scripts/run-memory-quality-lab.sh on baseline (current) and candidate (proposed fix) and produce a comparison report.
Read fixture files, report files, schemas, test files, and production source under apps/mobile/lib/ and services/realtime-agent/app/.
Suggest a rollback plan when a candidate is rejected.
may_not: Change, merge, deploy, or auto-apply code without human approval.
Change provider/model flags, retrieval thresholds, safety phrases, crisis rules, dependency rules, or VAD/endpointing configuration.
Use a real user dataset or send app/user content to any external model or API.
Claim a fix works without a green comparison between baseline and candidate.
Mark a proposal as improved unless scripts/run-memory-eval.sh passes AND all protected fixtures pass AND no P0/P1 regression appears.
Modify evaluation/memory/reports/ directly (reports are generated artifacts).
Access production databases, production logs, production rooms, production credentials, or real device/user identifiers.
Promote a fixture from proposed to protected without human maintainer acceptance.
Bypass the safe execution checks in run-memory-quality-lab.sh (production-target rejection, dry-run validation).

improvement_gate.description: A candidate fix is accepted as an improvement only when ALL of these pass.
conditions: Target failing fixture passes in the candidate run.
All fixtures marked protected: true pass in the candidate run.
No P0 or P1 regression appears in the baseline-vs-candidate comparison.
A human maintainer reviews and approves the code/config change.
